mechanism.summary: T066: replace the CLI process's global allocator (std System = macOS system malloc) with a thread-local size-class allocator that reuses freed blocks. 32 classes: 16-byte steps to 128 B, then four equal classes per power of two up to 8 KiB (160..8192); a layout larger than 8 KiB or with align > 16 stays System-managed, as do zero-sized layouts. Each thread keeps 32 free lists and per-class 64-KiB bump slabs from System; a freed block is pushed onto the freeing thread's list, so a cross-thread free transfers ownership without touching the allocating thread. realloc returns the same block inside one class, forwards to System.realloc only when both layouts are System-managed with equal alignment, and otherwise allocates the new layout, copies min(old,new) and deallocates the old block. alloc_zeroed zeroes layout.size() bytes of a recycled class block and forwards System-managed layouts. Slabs/free lists are retained until process exit and the const-initialized thread_local has no destructor, so no thread observes a destroyed pool. The allocator lives in qjs-cli; library crates and embedders keep their own allocator. Target selection used only each development program's exact-M allocator self-sample share and the frozen v6 payoff min(0.97,1/B_i); the T065 ablation is diagnostic priority evidence only and did not choose or order targets.
mechanism.generality: Admission is only a layout's size and alignment: any allocation up to 8 KiB with alignment at most 16 from any thread of the CLI process. No source text, bytecode, benchmark/library identity, path, checksum, iteration count or program shape is inspected; the same classes serve every allocation the engine or the workload makes, and the mechanism is the process-wide allocator contract rather than a workload-specific fast path.
semantic_risks: Every class block must be aligned to at least 16 bytes and at least layout.size() bytes usable; System-managed layouts must retain their exact requested align and be freed with the same layout they were allocated with.
realloc must preserve min(old,new) bytes across class changes and must not forward to System.realloc when the new layout changes alignment; a same-class realloc must keep the pointer and contents.
alloc_zeroed must clear recycled block content for layout.size() bytes; returning stale free-list pointers or unzeroed memory is a correctness bug.
Cross-thread frees only push into the freeing thread's list; no pointer may be pushed twice, and after thread exit retained blocks must never be reachable by another thread's live allocation.
TLS must stay usable from any thread at any point in its life; the pool is const-initialized with no destructor so nested/agent threads never observe destroyed TLS.
Out-of-memory must return null from every GlobalAlloc method (and System forward) rather than aborting inside the allocator; Rust's alloc error handler still owns the abort policy.

Instruction-blind mechanism: flat instructions do not waive wall or RSS costs, and the manual per-case median max-RSS candidate/M ceiling of 1.05 must be checked for every target and development case before promotion.
